### 📓 Docs Drift Check
⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b29f2dd117f4d105d9377aac39f2823bc0dc9e65` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

Main moved no file under `packages/mcp` or `ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer` since the merge-base.

Check-runs on this head, 48 in all, none failed. Completed green: Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Plan Test Core shards, filter, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, and the Test UI and Dogfood Regression Gate aggregates. Still running when read: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, the four Type Check jobs (source gates, workspace, debt ledger, consumer gates), Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure. The UI lanes, Build Docs and the queue verdicts are skipped by the path filter. The new test case has therefore no CI verdict yet: it runs in Test Core, and this PASS is on the text, not on those lanes.

### ① Derived judgments

The four points of the card, against the bullet in the tree (`DATASET_TOOL_LINES`, last entry, after "Choosing between a metric and an object query"):

1. Say the data does not record it and name what is missing: present ("say the data does not record it and name what is missing (say, a warranty end date)").
2. Offer the computation if the user supplies the parameter: present ("offer the computation if the user supplies it").
3. Never an assumed value or a conclusion drawn from one: present, with the measured shape quoted ("under a typical term, none would…"). Both measured answers fall under it: the first states an assumed term and concludes "none"; the second puts an example term inside the offer and concludes from it, which "nor draw a conclusion from one" names. Instruction text cannot guarantee the behaviour; the live re-run is the gallery task's, as the card says.
4. Volunteered figures come from a tool answer, as a cited source: the first half is present ("Any figure you add comes from a tool answer"); "as a cited source" is not. See S1.

Register: bold lead-in with a full stop, a colon-led case, imperatives, about six lines. It matches the three entries above it.

The test: not vacuous. With the bullet absent, `indexOf` returns -1 and the ordering assertion fails; the four substring assertions read a slice that starts at the bullet and ends at the next list item, and none of the four strings occurs in the heading that slice also takes in. The last assertion checks the render with no options does not carry the rule. See N1 for what it leaves unpinned.

Byte-identical render with no options: holds by construction. `DATASET_TOOL_LINES` has one use, `renderDatasetToolLines`, which returns the empty string unless `datasetTools` is true and the grant admits `data:read`; the other hunk is a comment.

Mirrors: none drifts. The Console copy (`ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts`) carries no dataset text and is pinned byte for byte against renders without the pair (`skill-md.test.ts`). `skill-md-surface-guard.test.ts` compares tool names, not prose. `content/docs/references/ai/dataset-tools.mdx` describes the shapes and does not restate the skill's rules. No other file at the head carries the selection rule's text or the new one.

### ② Semver level

Patch on the objectstack/mcp package is right: served instruction text for one host shape, no tool, schema, export or metadata moves. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand on both the changeset and the PR body; nothing in the tree contradicts either. Check Changeset was still running when read.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Landing tier: `check-governed-merges --pr 34140` at this file list reads NOT governed, 0 of 3 paths in the register, 33 changed lines. Ordinary queue landing. No face of the register touches this PR, so this record is the seat's choice, not a carrier the queue reads.
- Open question (dataset hosts only, or the always-on Conventions section): ruled A, keep it beside the dataset rule. The card asks for one bullet beside the dataset rule, both measured runs are dataset hosts, and the Conventions section is in the render the Console mirror must match byte for byte, which is outside this card's file surface. The rule's wording is not specific to datasets, so option B is a fair follow-up card on a measured instance from a host without the pair; it is not owed here.
- Eval: accepted. The tree has no eval set for the MCP door. The measuring question (`laptop_warranty_expiring`, truth `unanswerable`) is a case in `docs/qa/scenarios/asset_lifecycle.json`, and each of the other eight scenario cards carries an unanswerable case of its own.
- SQL push-down: not applicable, no query or join in the diff.
- Security: nothing found in this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

Proportionate: one bullet, one docblock sentence, one test case, one changeset. It does not contradict "No match: fall back to `query_records` / `aggregate_records` and say the answer is not from a governed metric": that line covers no metric match with an object that can answer, the new one covers nothing at all recording the value, and its opening clause ("No metric, object or field records…") states that order. It also sits with `membersWithheld` ("say so rather than saying the metric does not exist"), which keeps governing withheld measures.

No must-fix.

Should-fix:
- S1 · `skill-md.ts`, last sentence of the bullet. The card's fourth point is "figures you volunteer must come from a tool answer, as a cited source". The text says where a figure comes from and not that the answer names the source. Add the citation ("…comes from a tool answer; cite it"), in line with `query_dataset`'s "cite the source from it, not from memory".

Nits:
- N1 · `mcp-dataset-tools.test.ts`. The clause that targets the measured answer ("nor draw a conclusion from one") has no assertion, and `'comes from a tool'` stops before "answer" because of the line wrap. One more `toContain` closes the first.
- N2 · `skill-md.ts`. "say … (say, a warranty end date)" uses the word in two senses in one sentence; the entry above writes "such as".
- N3 · `skill-md.ts`. The example names the missing field of the measuring question, so that one case now reads its answer in the instructions. The other eight scenario cards still measure the rule cold; a neutral example would keep this one honest too.
- N4 · the changeset puts a paraphrase in quotation marks ("under a typical one-year warranty, none would expire"); the measured sentence reads differently.
- N5 · `skill-md.ts`. "the data does not record it" is said by a client that sees only what its identity may read; "the data you can read" would be exact for a narrowed grant. The card words it as the tree does, so this is the seat's call.
